note: The held-out state-lifecycle workloads, fixed before any candidate runs: sessions, families, lengths, counts, orders, salts, coverage rules and which requests are numerically scored targets. Prompts are contiguous spans of the hidden natural-text pool (infb_efficiency/pool.jsonl.xz, never shipped to the agent), tokenized with the checkpoint's tokenizer; each span's offset is a deterministic function of the seed, the family and the request's name, so a draw does not depend on how many requests ran before it. Turnover requests are setup traffic: their completion length, finiteness and engine health are checked, and they are not teacher-forced. Every other generated request is a scored target unless marked otherwise.
probe_note: eight different non-special token ids (each word one token, below the first special id 163584), none the public example's one-token prompt ('Hello', 19180); resolved with the checkpoint's tokenizer on 2026-10-01

metadata.rule: the private RPC infb_kda_metadata on every worker; each worker writes its own record (infb_kda_private/specification.json metadata)

d99.rule: turnover rounds until the ownership stream shows a reused state block on every replica (at most max_rounds); then each probe token id alone, 16 repeats, in repeat-major order. A probe whose state rows were never used before by another request is still scored; one more round runs (within the cap) and the same (token, repeat) is submitted next, at most coverage_waves times. Coverage: every (token, repeat) has a scored target on reused state storage.

continued.rule: 16 short prompts submitted together, then continued: fresh prefill of 2-3 tokens and valid one-token continuation rows, all scored

fresh_during_decode.rule: 16 streamed requests; after their first streamed output, one fresh one-token probe per probe token id, submitted together. Coverage: a step that schedules a fresh one-token probe beside running requests; up to coverage_waves waves.

dp_idle.rule: sequential requests, one at a time

dp_load.rule: each burst submitted together and drained; prompt lengths cycle across the bursts; then 17 streamed requests and, after their first output, 3 more, with the same length cycle

dp_coverage.rule: over the dp2 session's d99, continued, fresh, idle and load workloads: both replicas schedule real requests; at least one dummy/idle forward; at least one replayed graph extent above the replica's own padded live count; FULL graph replays observed on both replicas' ordinary decode; all eight workers' files

dp_quality.gsm8k: config.json infb.gsm8k (all 1,319 questions, the published floor)
dp_quality.fidelity: test_fidelity_against_model_author's protocol and bars on the hidden 36 sequences

a1.rule: cold prompts at each length, each with its own salt; for each hit prefix P, warm P + one suffix token, then P + another, sharing the case salt; the second must consume the completed prefix at len(P)

a6.rule: warm the three prefixes as in a1 (case salt), then one wave of 8 hits cycling the prefixes with new suffixes (case salt) and 8 fresh prompts cycling the fresh lengths (own salts)

a2.rule: warm prefix + one suffix token; then the branches prefix + suffix_i executed in order, all in the case salt; each must restore the retained prefix state equal to the producer's

a3.rule: a blocker prompt (blocker tokens, its first token unlike the prefix's, greedy, ignore_eos, scored by nothing) is streamed first; once its first token arrives the engine is in steady decode, and the eight cold siblings go as ONE /v1/completions carrying eight token-ID prompts (case salt), so they are admitted at one step boundary rather than by arrival jitter; the blocker is cancelled once the eight complete; then one more sibling after they complete; no restore of a state not completed in an earlier step, and the follow-up must reuse the prefix

a4.rule: each long prompt alone (case salt), its prefill chunks recorded; then siblings sharing its first k tokens plus a new suffix; each sibling must restore the largest completed boundary at or below k that the native trace records as produced and retained

a5.rule: prompt of 4B+1 generating 576; later prompts are the prompt plus the first (k - 2049) generated tokens plus a new suffix (case salt); each must restore the largest completed boundary at or below k, and at k >= 2560 that boundary lies in generated history

binding.rule: per (layer, views) pass, its own salt: warm prefix + s0; control prefix + s1 (no intervention); then in a second salt warm prefix + s0, target prefix + s1 with the intervention at its restore, then sibling prefix + s2. The target's continuation must differ from the control's; the sibling must restore the producer's state bitwise. The perturbed target is not a scored target.

p1.rule: warm prefix + s0; prefix + s1 must hit; 32 distinct fill prompts submitted together; turnover: a block of the warm prefix freshly allocated to another request; then prefix + s0 again (a miss is valid after eviction); then prefix + s2 must hit. Up to coverage_waves fills to observe the turnover.

p2.rule: 16 unique prompts submitted together (case salt), up to coverage_waves waves; case 2: a resumed request with prior output > 0 and history % 512 != 0; case 3: among qualifying resumed requests whose completed boundary is retained at wave end, the earliest by (step, batch row); its largest retained completed boundary strictly below its final computed count; a branch of that history prefix plus a new suffix must restore it

p4.rule: 16 streamed requests (case salt); the four named are cancelled through the client disconnect after their first output; after the rest complete, four fresh one-token requests (probe ids 0..3) and two branches from the earliest-finished unaffected request whose 1,024-token boundary is retained; cancelled requests must finish and leave scheduling; their partial outputs are scored
